blind_rationale: (1) SWiM Family fit (`none_nonfit`): The paper's headline empirical tests examine political elite capture via politician residential location (`GP head's village` in Table 5; `Politician road` in Table 6) and social-group residential sorting (`SC/ST road`, `Mixed caste road`, `Muslim road` vs upper-caste roads in Table 6), alongside demographic/literacy predictors of Gram Panchayat (GP) task-responsibility awareness (Table 4). Political patronage based on where an elected village politician lives and residential caste stratification do not correspond to SWiM Family A (formal legal status, land tenure, legal recognition, or formal governance rules), Family B (external assistance, citizen participation, or trust interventions), or Family C (public/private ownership, regulatory enforcement, or utility institutional capacity). Two secondary covariates touch adjacent family concepts—`Oligarchy` (informal concentration of village governance power, conceptually adjacent to Family A) and `GP HQ in village` (administrative seat location within a multi-village GP, conceptually adjacent to Family C administrative structure)—but `Oligarchy` suffers a publisher typesetting defect in Table 5 (missing point estimates, reported in text p. 695 as making no difference) and `GP HQ in village` is statistically null across all four road-sanitation outcomes in Table 5 (significant only for non-WASH road paving, +0.047**, SE 0.021, and Table 4 awareness of water-tank cleaning, +0.127***, SE 0.047). Excluding this study from Families A, B, and C as `none_nonfit` is therefore substantively justified. (2) Scope check for Narrow Criterion 2 (`borderline_governance_or_proxy`, flag for `E03` review): Although Section II discusses the 1992 Constitutional Amendment (PRI Act) sanitation mandate and Tamil Nadu's Public Health Act / Panchayats Act 1994, no legal or regulatory rule is empirically tested in the reported regressions: state/district legal differences are absorbed by block fixed effects (Tables 4–5) and village fixed effects (Table 6), while statutory GP presidency reservation (for women or SC/ST/backward castes) is included only as an unreported control variable. The tested exposures (`GP head's village`, `Politician road`, `GP HQ in village`, `Oligarchy`) are de facto political-capture and administrative-seat proxies rather than legal rules governing access. (3) Scope check for Criterion 4 (`borderline_institutional_or_compliance_outcome`, flag for `E04` review): No household drinking-water or toilet/latrine access outcome is measured (Note 11 explicitly notes private toilets under the Total Sanitation Campaign were not evaluated). Table 4 measures GP members' institutional role awareness (failing C4), `Road is paved` measures transport infrastructure (failing C4), and the remaining outcomes in Tables 5–6 (`Road has drain`, `Road is moderately clean`, `No garbage on road`, `Road has unclogged drain`) measure GP performance in public street-sweeping and roadside stormwater/wastewater drainage along village roads rather than household water or sanitation service access.

headline_estimate_summary: Linear probability models (OLS) with clustered SEs; no 95% CIs or exact p-values are printed (only star thresholds; note also that Taylor & Francis font encoding renders minus signs as leading '7' in raw text extraction of Tables 4-6, verified against text). (1) Inter-village political capture (Table 5, PDF p. 11 / p. 694; block FE, colony-clustered SEs, controlling for unreported GP reservation status, fraction landless, number of castes, GP head age/education/wealth/experience, and road characteristics): `GP head's village` (vs non-head village in same block) predicts `Road has drain` b = +0.053*** (SE 0.015, p < 0.01, N = 8,452), `Road is paved` b = +0.028* (SE 0.016, p < 0.10, N = 8,452), `Road is moderately clean` b = +0.037** (SE 0.015, p < 0.05, N = 8,398), `No garbage on road` b = +0.060*** (SE 0.018, p < 0.01, N = 8,407), and `Road has unclogged drain (cond)` b = -0.017 (SE 0.024, NS, N = 2,038). In the same Table 5, `GP HQ in village` is null on all sanitation outcomes (`Road has drain` +0.022 [SE 0.021], `Road is moderately clean` -0.027 [SE 0.018], `No garbage on road` -0.021 [SE 0.023], `Road has unclogged drain` +0.004 [SE 0.031]) and positive only for `Road is paved` (+0.047**, SE 0.021); `Oligarchy` has a printing defect in Table 5 (two parenthesized rows, no stars; text p. 695 states no difference). (2) Intra-village political capture & social exclusion (Table 6, PDF p. 13 / p. 696; village FE, colony-clustered SEs; note footnote says *10%/**5%/***1% but t-ratios match *5%/**1%/***0.1%): `Politician road` (politician lives on road vs other roads in same village) predicts `Road has drain` b = +0.078*** (SE 0.020, N = 10,026), `Road paved` b = +0.052* (SE 0.021, N = 10,026), `Road is moderately clean` b = +0.055*** (SE 0.016, N = 9,971), `No garbage on road` b = -0.006 (SE 0.018, NS, N = 9,976), and `Road with unclogged drain (cond)` b = +0.003 (SE 0.020, NS, N = 2,244). `SC/ST road` (vs upper-caste road) predicts `Road has drain` +0.015 (SE 0.015), `Road paved` -0.051** (SE 0.016), `Road is moderately clean` +0.001 (SE 0.014), `No garbage on road` -0.032* (SE 0.013), and `Road with unclogged drain` -0.025 (SE 0.023). (3) GP responsibility awareness (Table 4, PDF p. 10 / p. 693; village-level LPM with block FE, GP-clustered SEs, N = 323 to 437): `GP head's village` is null across all 7 tasks; `GP HQ in village` predicts higher awareness only for `Cleaning drinking water tanks` (+0.127***, SE 0.047, N = 372); `Oligarchy` predicts lower awareness of `Spraying for mosquitoes` (-0.340**, SE 0.168, N = 425) and `Cleaning drinking water tanks` (-0.467*, SE 0.238, N = 372) but higher awareness of `Road cleaning` (+0.378**, SE 0.183, N = 437).
study_design_and_sample: Cross-sectional multi-stage observational survey and direct field-investigator road observation study in rural South India (4 states: Andhra Pradesh, Karnataka, Kerala, Tamil Nadu; purposively sampled districts/blocks, random sampling of 201 Gram Panchayats and 527 villages/wards [Note 6 state breakdown sums to 506], and 10,408 mapped village roads), combining 2003 GP member interviews and direct road observations with 2002 village census/participatory appraisal data. Analytic sample sizes: Table 4 village-level awareness LPMs N = 323 to 437 villages; Table 5 inter-village road-level LPMs (block fixed effects) N = 8,452 roads (`Road has drain`, `Road is paved`), N = 8,398 (`Road is moderately clean`), N = 8,407 (`No garbage on road`), and N = 2,038 conditional roads with drains (`Road has unclogged drain`); Table 6 intra-village road-level LPMs (village fixed effects) N = 10,026 (`Road has drain`, `Road paved`), N = 9,971 (`Road is moderately clean`), N = 9,976 (`No garbage on road`), and N = 2,244 conditional roads with drains.
